# 2 Kings Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 224v–226r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_004_page_001.jpg, 2KI_004_page_002.jpg, 2KI_004_page_003.jpg, 2KI_004_page_004.jpg

---

**4:1** And-a-woman, one from-the-wives of-the-sons of-the-prophets, cried-out to Elisha, saying: Your-servant my-husband is-dead, and-you know that your-servant was a-fearer of-YHWH. And-the-creditor [ha-nosheh] has-come to-take my-two children [yeladay] to-him as-slaves ['avadim].

**4:2** And-said to-her Elisha: What shall-I-do for-you? Tell me — what do-you-have in-the-house? And-she-said: Your-maidservant has-nothing at-all in-the-house except a-flask [asukh] of-oil [shamen].

**4:3** And-he-said: Go, ask for-yourself vessels [kelim] from-outside, from all your-neighbors — empty vessels [kelim reqim]. Do-not let-them-be-few [al tam'iti].

**4:4** And-go-in and-shut the-door behind-you and-behind your-sons, and-pour into all these vessels, and-the-full-one set-aside.

**4:5** And-she-went from-him and-shut the-door behind-her and-behind her-sons. They [were] bringing [the vessels] near to-her, and-she [was] pouring.

**4:6** And-it-was when-the-vessels were-full, and-she-said to-her-son: Bring-near to-me yet a-vessel. And-he-said to-her: There-is-no more vessel. And-the-oil stopped [vaya'amod].

**4:7** And-she-came and-told the-man of-God, and-he-said: Go, sell the-oil and-pay your-debt [nishyekh], and-you and-your-sons shall-live on-the-rest.

**4:8** And-it-was one-day, and-passed Elisha to-Shunem, and-there [was] a-great woman [ishah gedolah], and-she-seized-him [vatachazaq bo] to-eat bread. And-it-was whenever-he-passed, he-turned-aside there to-eat bread.

**4:9** And-she-said to her-husband: Behold, please, I-know that a-holy man of-God [ish elohim qadosh] he [is], passing over-us continually.

**4:10** Let-us-make, please, a-small upper-room [aliyyat qir qetannah] of-wall, and-let-us-set for-him there a-bed and-a-table and-a-chair and-a-lamp [menorah], and-it-shall-be when-he-comes to-us, he-shall-turn-aside there.

**4:11** And-it-was one-day, and-he-came there, and-he-turned-aside to the-upper-room and-lay-down there.

**4:12** And-he-said to-Gechazi his-servant [na'aro]: Call to-this Shunammite-woman. And-he-called-her, and-she-stood before-him.

**4:13** And-he-said to-him: Say, please, to-her: Behold, you-have-trembled [charadti] for-us [with] all this trembling [charedah]. What is-to-be-done for-you? Is-there to-speak for-you to the-king or to the-commander of-the-army? And-she-said: In-the-midst of-my-people I-am-dwelling [yoshavet].

**4:14** And-he-said: And-what is-to-be-done for-her? And-said Gechazi: Indeed [aval], a-son she-has-not, and-her-husband [is] old.

**4:15** And-he-said: Call-her. And-he-called-her, and-she-stood in-the-doorway [ba-petach].

**4:16** And-he-said: At-this appointed-time [la-mo'ed ha-zeh], at-the-living-season [ka-'et chayyah], you shall-be-embracing [chobeqet] a-son. And-she-said: No, my-lord, man of-God — do-not deceive [al tekhazzev] your-maidservant!

**4:17** And-conceived the-woman and-bore a-son at-that appointed-time, at-the-living-season, that Elisha had-spoken to-her.

**4:18** And-grew the-child. And-it-was one-day, and-he-went-out to his-father, to the-reapers.

**4:19** And-he-said to his-father: My-head, my-head [roshi roshi]! And-he-said to the-servant: Carry-him to his-mother.

**4:20** And-he-carried-him and-brought-him to his-mother, and-he-sat upon her-knees until the-noon [ha-tsohorayim], and-he-died.

**4:21** And-she-went-up and-laid-him upon the-bed of-the-man of-God, and-shut [the door] upon-him and-went-out.

**4:22** And-she-called to her-husband and-said: Send, please, to-me one of-the-servants and-one of-the-donkeys, and-I-will-run to the-man of-God and-return.

**4:23** And-he-said: Why are-you going to-him today? It-is-not new-moon [chodesh] and-not Sabbath [shabbat]. And-she-said: Shalom [peace].

**4:24** And-she-saddled the-donkey and-said to her-servant: Drive and-go! Do-not restrain [al ta'atsor] the-riding for-me unless I-say to-you.

**4:25** And-she-went and-came to the-man of-God, to-Mount Carmel. And-it-was when-the-man of-God saw-her from-afar, and-he-said to-Gechazi his-servant: Behold — the-Shunammite, this-one.

**4:26** Now, run, please, to-meet-her and-say to-her: Is-it-well [ha-shalom] with-you? Is-it-well with-your-husband? Is-it-well with-the-child? And-she-said: Shalom.

**4:27** And-she-came to the-man of-God, to the-mountain, and-she-seized his-feet [vatachazaq be-raglav]. And-drew-near Gechazi to-push-her-away [lehodphah], and-said the-man of-God: Leave-her-alone [harpeh lah], for her-soul [nafshah] [is] bitter [marah] in-her, and-YHWH has-hidden [he'elim] [it] from-me and-has-not told-me.

**4:28** And-she-said: Did-I-ask a-son from my-lord? Did-I-not say, do-not deceive me?

**4:29** And-he-said to-Gechazi: Gird your-loins and-take my-staff [mish'anti] in-your-hand and-go. If you-meet a-man, do-not greet-him; and-if a-man greets-you, do-not answer-him. And-place my-staff upon the-face of-the-boy.

**4:30** And-said the-mother of-the-boy: As-YHWH-lives and-as-your-soul-lives, I-will-not leave-you. And-he-arose and-went after-her.

**4:31** And-Gechazi passed before-them and-placed the-staff upon the-face of-the-boy, and-there-was-no voice [qol] and-no attention [qashev]. And-he-returned to-meet-him and-told-him, saying: The-boy has-not awakened.

**4:32** And-came Elisha to-the-house, and-behold the-boy [was] dead, laid upon his-bed.

**4:33** And-he-went-in and-shut the-door behind the-two-of-them and-prayed [vayitpallel] to YHWH.

**4:34** And-he-went-up and-lay upon the-child and-placed his-mouth upon his-mouth and-his-eyes upon his-eyes and-his-palms upon his-palms, and-he-stretched [vayighar] upon-him, and-the-flesh of-the-child became-warm [vayacham].

**4:35** And-he-returned and-walked in-the-house, once here and-once there, and-went-up and-stretched upon-him. And-sneezed [vayezorer] the-boy seven times [sheva pe'amim], and-opened the-boy his-eyes.

**4:36** And-he-called to-Gechazi and-said: Call to-this Shunammite-woman. And-he-called-her, and-she-came to-him. And-he-said: Take-up your-son.

**4:37** And-she-came and-fell at his-feet and-bowed to-the-ground, and-she-took-up her-son and-went-out.

**4:38** And-Elisha returned to-the-Gilgal, and-the-famine [was] in-the-land. And-the-sons of-the-prophets [were] sitting before-him, and-he-said to-his-servant: Set-on the-great pot [ha-sir ha-gedolah] and-cook stew [nazid] for-the-sons of-the-prophets.

**4:39** And-one went-out to the-field to-gather herbs [orot], and-he-found a-wild vine [gefen sadeh] and-gathered from-it gourds of-the-field [paqqo'ot sadeh], his-garment full, and-he-came and-sliced [vayefalach] [them] into the-pot of-stew, for they-did-not know [them].

**4:40** And-they-poured-out for-the-men to-eat, and-it-was as-they-ate from-the-stew, and-they cried-out and-said: Death in-the-pot [mavet ba-sir], man of-God! And-they-could-not eat.

**4:41** And-he-said: Then-bring flour [qemach]. And-he-cast [it] into the-pot and-said: Pour-out for-the-people and-let-them-eat. And-there-was no harmful-thing [davar ra'] in-the-pot.

**4:42** And-a-man came from-Ba'al-Shalishah and-brought to-the-man of-God bread of-the-firstfruits [lechem bikkurim], twenty loaves of-barley and-fresh-grain [karmel] in-his-sack [be-tsiqlon]. And-he-said: Give to-the-people and-let-them-eat.

**4:43** And-said his-servant: How shall-I-set this before a-hundred men? And-he-said: Give to-the-people and-let-them-eat, for thus says YHWH: They-shall-eat and-have-left-over [vehother].

**4:44** And-he-set [it] before-them, and-they-ate and-had-left-over, according-to-the-word of-YHWH.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — ha-nosheh:** The creditor. Debt slavery was legal under Israelite law (Exod 21:2-7; Lev 25:39-43) but was supposed to be limited to six years. The widow's desperation shows the system's failure to protect the vulnerable.

**v.8 — ishah gedolah:** "A great woman" — great in social standing and wealth, not physical stature. She is never named; she is identified only by her town (Shunem) and her greatness.

**v.13 — "In the midst of my people I am dwelling":** She refuses political patronage. She needs nothing from the king or the army; her sufficiency is in her community. This is an act of dignified independence.

**v.16 — ka-'et chayyah:** The same phrase used in Gen 18:10 when the angels announce Sarah's son. The Shunammite echo of Sarah is deliberate; her "Do not deceive" echoes Sarah's laughter.

**v.34 — mouth upon mouth:** The body-to-body resuscitation echoes Elijah's raising of the widow's son (1 Kgs 17:21). The double prophet, the double miracle.

**v.42-44 — Feeding the hundred:** Twenty barley loaves feed a hundred men with leftovers. The verbal echoes with Jesus' feeding miracles (John 6:9-13) are striking.

*— EMET*
